reason: B provides the stronger, more testable proposal because it uses matched wear-only and corrosion-only controls, tests for degradation beyond their additive effects, predicts changes in both responses, and measures oxide integrity. Its main weakness is that a chloride “solution” at 600–900 °C is physically ill-defined unless specified as a molten salt or pressurized medium, and the cited evidence supports tribo-oxide disruption more directly than galvanic pitting.
